statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains at its floor through the final hour of the CME equity-index halt, while Stress stays elevated on a Brent six-week high set against visible demand-side offsets.
recommendation: Path risk in this window is concentrated in the single hour after futures matching resumes at 22:00Z. Outside that window the mapped state remains green with Tail well below the block threshold.
headline: Last hour of the Labor Day halt; Brent's six-week high is offset by SPR and Chinese demand data, leaving the 22:00Z restart as the one mapped danger window
body: CME equity-index futures have been halted since 17:00Z and resume matching at 22:00Z for the Tuesday trade date, while NYSE, Nasdaq and the US bond market stayed shut all day for Labor Day and reopen at 13:30Z tomorrow. NQ's last print is unchanged at 29,565.25, up 40.50 points (+0.14%), inside a narrow 29,530.50-29,682.50 holiday range it had already faded from, so the pre-halt tape showed working retracements and no one-way structure. With no order book there is no price path capable of denying mean reversion, which is why Tail sits at its floor; the same absence is what caps a forward read. No new Middle East headline has landed since the 15:55 ET update in which the Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of airstrikes, including one on a prison in Al-Hazm that killed seven, with fighting intensifying near the Bab al-Mandab strait. The material addition this hour is on the energy demand side. Brent last traded near 96.944, up 0.69%, after reaching about 97.50 on Monday, a six-week high and nearly 40% above pre-war levels; WTI October settled at 91.48, up 0.20%, after fading from a 93.29 session high. Trading Economics attributes the failure to rebound further to major economies drawing on inventory: the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve has fallen below 290 million barrels, its lowest since 1982, while China has significantly cut crude imports and refinery runs. That is a genuine counterweight to the supply-side escalation narrative and it is why Stress holds at 63 rather than extending. Reports that Aramco facilities were hit in fresh attacks on Monday, and that Iran is close to agreeing a tanker route through the Strait of Hormuz with Oman, remain the two open threads. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright has said Washington will maintain its naval presence and blockade, and Hormuz transits are down to roughly ten vessels a day against about 130 before the war. The macro backdrop is a separate and independent channel. Friday's August payrolls came in at 162,000 against roughly 55,000 expected with unemployment at 4.1%, pushing odds of a September Fed rate increase to about 58% and lifting the two-year yield to its highest since January 2025; the Dow fell 0.51%, the S&P 500 0.38% to 7,718.60 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.29% to 26,506.99. US Treasury cash markets were closed today, so the most recent H.15 values remain those for 3 September, 4.34% at two years and 4.77% at ten. VIX last traded near 15.30, historically calm. The single concentrated risk is the 22:00Z restart, where roughly five hours of unpriced escalation would meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. That hour alone is mapped to WATCH; path risk then decays through Asia and rises again modestly into the 13:30Z cash reopen. All post-halt structure is described conditionally because none of it is observable at the assessment cutoff.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the last twenty-four hourly Claude assessments are available; the 2026-09-06T21:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. The window was uniformly green with EA_ON throughout and Tail confined to a 5-10% band. Stress ran at 54-57% through the Asian and European sessions, rose to 61-64% across the US afternoon as crude extended and holiday liquidity thinned, and has held at 62-63% since the 17:00Z halt. Confidence fell from 86% to 75% over the stretch as live price evidence disappeared with the halt. Dominant mode was normal apart from the 14:00Z, 16:00Z and 17:00Z slots, which were mixed while the energy-versus-equity divergence widened.
outlookSummary: The next twenty-four hours are governed by market structure rather than macro. Futures stay halted for the remainder of this hour, so the opening forecast slot carries no tradable path and Tail sits at its floor. The one elevated slot is the 22:00Z restart, where several hours of unpriced escalation would meet the thinnest liquidity of the window; that hour alone maps to WATCH. Path risk then decays through the Asian and European sessions as depth rebuilds, with a secondary rise into the 13:30Z US cash reopen, the first regular session after the three-day weekend and the first full-depth pricing of both the weekend tanker exchange and Friday's hawkish payroll surprise. The energy channel is more balanced than it was earlier in the day: Brent's six-week high is set against a US SPR below 290 million barrels and materially lower Chinese imports and refinery runs, which is why Stress is projected to normalise rather than extend. All post-halt structure is framed conditionally because none of it is observable at the assessment cutoff; only the pre-halt range, its fade, and crude's retracement from its session highs are stated as fact. NFIB at 10:00Z and the weekly ADP print at 12:15Z are the only scheduled US releases inside the window, with the 3-year auction at 17:00Z as a rates checkpoint and PPI and claims on Thursday and CPI on Friday as the week's principal events.
